extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of anthropology/ethnology; scholars interested in comparative ritual and ceremonial practices
extracted.subtask_description: A scholarly/popular‑science essay surveying cross‑cultural practices (hair cutting, circumcision, tattooing, blood‑letting, scars, and related mutilations) and interpreting their social, political, and religious meanings—especially links to servitude, status, propitiation, and apotheosis. The text assembles ethnographic and historical examples to support theoretical claims about origins and functions of these rites.
